original.target_description: Experiment 1 on printed pp. 266–267: several overall, chance-level and block-specific grammaticality-sensitivity tests; p. 3 alone does not identify the requested test.

notes: Identity independently verified from the document itself: title The impact of adjacent-dependencies and staged-input on the learnability of center-embedded hierarchical structures; Jun Lai and Fenna H. Poletiek; Cognition 118 (2011), 265–273; doi:10.1016/j.cognition.2010.11.011. Supplied canonical text is a full primary journal article, including experiments, discussion, appendix and references, rather than an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied. Only n_o and es_value_o are assigned; all other fields are unassigned placeholders. The sole locator p. 3 corresponds to printed p. 267, Experiment 1, but supplies no outcome/test discriminator. Candidates include the overall SS versus random comparison (t (26) = 3.94, p = .001), SS versus chance (t (13) = 4.21, p = .001), SS Block 12 versus Block 1 (t (13) = 2.59, p < .05), random-group change (t (13) = negative .98, n.s.), Block 1 between groups (t (26) = 1.98, n.s.), and Block 12 between groups (t (26) = 2.87, p < .01). These are candidates, not selected statistics. The 28 students in section 2.1.1 are a participant total; this does not establish the analytic N for every candidate test. No group sizes are inferred from degrees of freedom and no N sum is performed. Section 2.2 prints d-prime sensitivity means, accuracy and t tests, not Cohen's d; footnote 5 explicitly identifies the sensitivity metric. No effect-size conversion was performed. Row target remains ambiguous.
